Slender arched bridges of pale carved stone span between the towers, their railings worked into flowing leaf-and-vine patterns.
Glowing lanterns like captured starlight hang from the branches and balconies, casting soft silver light across the walkways.
Living trees have been grown into the architecture itself, their boughs forming arches and their roots flowing into stairs.
Delicate spiral staircases wind upward around living trunks, each step carved from pale moonstone and edged with silver filigree.
Gossamer banners of woven silk drift from every spire, their surfaces shimmering with embroidered constellations and elvish runes.
Vine-wrapped balconies overhang the lower streets, fragrant blossoms cascading down in curtains of white and pale gold.
Glowing crystal lamps are set into the walls at intervals, pulsing with a soft inner light like breathing embers.
Reflecting pools mirror the towers and sky above, their surfaces ringed with carved lotus motifs and smooth white stone.
Graceful fountains send arcs of water singing through the air, their basins etched with scenes from elven legend.
Tall statues of ancient elf-lords stand at every gate, carved in flowing robes with expressions of serene wisdom.
Flowering creepers blanket the lower walls entirely, threading through carved lattice and erupting in cascades of violet bloom.
Thin elegant spires rise at every corner, their tips capped with glowing amber crystals visible for many miles.
Woven-branch archways form natural tunnels along the garden paths, the living wood trained for centuries into graceful curves.
Carved-leaf stonework covers every lintel and column, each individual leaf undercut so finely the stone appears to tremble.
Narrow footbridges of woven silver wire and pale timber connect high platforms among the canopy, swaying gently in the breeze.
Tall windows are filled with panes of translucent sea-green glass, casting cool dappled patterns across the polished floors within.
Intricate mosaic paths wind through every courtyard, their tiles depicting birds, deer, and flowing rivers in vivid natural colour.
Slender columns of pale marble are carved to resemble bundled saplings, their capitals blooming into stone flowers at the ceiling.
Open-air libraries occupy tiered terraces, their shelves carved directly into the living wood of enormous ancient trees.
Delicate iron weathervanes shaped like soaring eagles and dragons crown every roof peak, turning silently in the high wind.
Ornate wooden doors are carved in deep relief with forest scenes, their surfaces polished to a warm honeyed glow.
Suspended gardens hang from the undersides of high platforms, trailing roots and blossoms downward like living chandeliers of green.
Stone benches line every walkway, their surfaces softened with moss cushions and carved along the sides with running deer.
Curved roof eaves sweep upward at the corners like outstretched wings, their undersides painted in deep forest green and gold.
Soft chimes of hollow silver tubes hang at every doorway, singing quietly whenever the wind moves through the city.
